findings.title: Calling `commit` from a background thread violates Arroyo/confluent-kafka thread safety
findings.body: `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy` spawns a background `commit_thread` that calls `self.commit_function(committable)`, which invokes the Arroyo `Commit` callback passed into `create_with_partitions`. In Arroyo's `StreamProcessor`, that callback calls `self.__consumer.stage_positions(...)` and `self.__consumer.commit(...)` on the underlying `KafkaConsumer` (and `confluent_kafka.Consumer`), while the main processor thread is concurrently calling `poll()` / `stage_positions()` on the same consumer and unsynchronized internal dicts (`__PartitionState.__staged_offsets`). Arroyo strategies are expected to invoke `commit` from `poll()`, `submit()`, or `join()` on the main consumer thread. Calling `commit` from a separate thread introduces data races on Arroyo's offset state and concurrent calls into the librdkafka consumer.

findings.title: `close()` and `terminate()` shut down the shared `FixedQueuePool`, breaking partition rebalances
findings.body: `ResultsStrategyFactory` creates a single `self.queue_pool` in `__init__` and reuses it across every `create_with_partitions` call. In Arroyo, whenever partitions are revoked or rebalanced, the active strategy has `close()`/`join()` (or `terminate()`) called on it, and `create_with_partitions` is then called again to build a new strategy instance. Because `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` and `terminate()` call `self.queue_pool.shutdown()` (which permanently shuts down all queues and stops all worker threads), the first rebalance will leave `self.queue_pool` dead: subsequent `submit()` calls on the newly created strategy will raise `queue.ShutDown` (caught and immediately marked completed in `submit()`), silently dropping all messages and committing their offsets without processing.

findings.title: Work queues are unbounded and `submit()` never raises `MessageRejected`, allowing unbounded memory growth
findings.body: In `FixedQueuePool.__init__`, each `queue.Queue()` is created with `maxsize=0` (unbounded), and `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.submit` never raises Arroyo's `MessageRejected`. Although the class docstring claims "Natural backpressure when queues fill up", the main consumer loop will read from Kafka at full speed and buffer an arbitrary number of `WorkItem` objects (each retaining the raw `Message` and decoded payload) in memory if any worker falls behind, risking OOM kills and also failing to flush remaining queued items on shutdown because `worker.shutdown = True` causes workers to exit their loop on the next iteration instead of draining the queue.

findings.title: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown` sets `worker.shutdown = True` before draining, dropping queued items and skipping final commit
findings.body: `FixedQueuePool.shutdown()` sets `worker.shutdown = True` on all workers and then calls `q.shutdown(immediate=False)`. Because `OrderedQueueWorker.run` checks `while not self.shutdown:`, any worker that finishes its current item sees `self.shutdown == True` and exits immediately instead of draining the remaining items in `work_queue` (which `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` is meant to allow). Furthermore, `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` stops `commit_thread` before calling `queue_pool.shutdown()` and never performs a final commit afterwards, so offsets for items completed during shutdown are never committed.
